newsitem.title: HONDURAS: 22, mostly Hondurans, feared drowned after boats capsize.
newsitem.headline: 22, mostly Hondurans, feared drowned after boats capsize.

text.p: Twenty-two people, mostly Honduran farm workers, were feared drowned after two boats taking them from Belize to Honduras capsized in a storm, authorities said on Wednesday.

"We've got two patrol boats looking for survivors, but chances are slim any of them are still alive," Capt. Juan Rodriguez, head of the naval base in the northern Honduran port of Puerto Cortes, told Reuters.
He said the small boats might have crashed on Belize's coral reef, the second longest in the world.
One boat, the Denovve, was found by fisherman near Puerto Cortes on Sunday with no survivors aboard and was towed to land.

Leticia de Ramirez, Honduran vice consul in Belize, told Tegucigalpa's Radio America in a telephone interview: "I have received the bad news from Belizean authorities about these two boats carrying 22 people. No trace of these people has been found."
She said the Denovve had 15 aboard, including two Belizeans, and left Belize on July 8. The other, the Nancy, carried seven, including one Belizean. It left port on July 12.
Most of the passengers were Hondurans who had been harvesting bananas in Belize and were on their way home to Puerto Cortes.
